correctness.rationale: The corrected final proof was reconstructed at exponent level. Achilles means every exponent >=2 and exponent gcd 1, so at least one exponent is odd. The principal layer has a unique form p^(2j+1)m^2 with j>=1, p not dividing squarefree m, omega(m)=r-1; it is automatically Achilles. Fixed-order Landau counting for m gives the main term, and on the polylogarithmic truncation log Y=(1/2+o(1))log X, producing the factor 2. The absolutely convergent weight sum is sum_p p^(-3/2)/(1-p^-1). Uniform exclusion of the distinguished prime is lower order. Every nonprincipal pattern has at least two exceptional exponents; summing their p^(-e/2) weights leaves one fewer Landau loglog degree for r>=3, while r=2 is O(X^(1/3+o(1))). Thus the remainder is lower order. The finite verifier's 10^8 enumeration is corroborative only. The ready repair restores TeX control-sequence bytes in RESULT.md without changing the mathematics.
risks: The proof uses standard fixed-k Landau asymptotics and uniform upper bounds rather than reproving them.
No effective error term or growing-r uniformity is supplied.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies the first non-perfect-power layer inside a classical thin multiplicative set and resolves every fixed number of distinct prime factors with one explicit universal prime-series constant. It explains how removing the dominant square layer changes the fixed-r scale and is a natural asymptotic classification, not a recomputation of a finite table.
risks: The result is local in fixed r and does not replace global distribution results for omega.
